cassia_summary.reasoning_short: The annotation correctly identifies the dominant signal in the marker list as B-cell lineage. The top-ranked markers include TCL1A, IGHM, CD79A, CD79B, CD22, CD37, POU2AF1, STAP1, FCER2, P2RX5, P2RY10, and immunoglobulin gene segments; these are canonical and mutually reinforcing. It appropriately checks alternative lineages: no CD3/TRAC for T cells, no NKG7/GNLY for NK, no LYZ/CD14 for myeloid, no MZB1/XBP1/SDC1 for plasma cells. This is a good example of balanced marker interpretation and not over-focusing on one gene. The subtyping as mature/naive IgM+ B cells is reasonable, since TCL1A, FCER2/CD23, IGHM, CD22, and CD79A/B co-occur, while memory/plasma cells would typically downregulate TCL1A and CD23. The transitional possibility is also plausible in tissue context. The annotation also acknowledges the presence of pancreatic epithelial/acinar/stromal genes (GATA4, KRT4, PIGR, CPA5, COL19A1) and explains them as ambient RNA or doublets, which is thoughtful and avoids misclassifying the cluster as epithelium. Weaknesses: The annotation could be more critical about whether the pancreatic markers are contamination vs. a genuine mixed/doublet population, since several are within the top 50 and not all are trivial background. Also, IGHE is present; while the annotation mentions it, it is somewhat incompatible with a pure naive IgM+ B-cell interpretation and should have been more explicitly considered (e.g., possible contaminating switched B cells, ambient immunoglobulin RNA, or a small IgE+ subset). The three sub-cell types are not fully mutually exclusive, and the confidence in “activated/mature B cells” is lower, but this is presented as less likely. Overall, the main cell type is correct and the reasoning is well-balanced; these caveats prevent a perfect score.

enrich_summary.reasoning_short: Top markers include canonical B-cell markers (CD79A, CD79B, CD37, CD22) and memory B-cell markers (TCL1A, SGO2, POU2AF1, FCER2, STAP1, P2RX5, IGHM, IGKJ5, IGHE). Especially TCL1A and SGO2 are strongly associated with memory B cells. The enrichment terms are dominated by broad metabolism and genetic processing, which are common in activated or memory B cells. The absence of T-cell-specific markers (CD3D, CD3E, CD4, CD8A) and NK-cell markers (FCGR3A, FGFBP2) rules out T/NK identities. The presence of IGJ and other immunoglobulin genes supports a B-cell lineage, and the combination of TCL1A and SGO2 with CD27 (though CD27 not listed, the combination of markers is sufficient) points specifically to memory B cells.
